question: Can causal factors produce an effect if they are entirely separate in nature from it?
premises: Agents and other causal factors may be posited.
These factors may be separate from the effect.
Separation raises doubt about their capacity to constitute the effect.
inference: If causal factors are wholly separate in nature, their role in producing the effect is problematic.
plain_english: If agents and other factors are separate and of a nature distinct from it, can they be so?
